name: Prostate (BPH / Prostate Cancer)
remarks: Synthea Generic Module Framework state machine for the prostate pathway in males aged 50-60.
CLINICAL MODEL (agreed with domain expert): BPH is NOT modelled as a precursor of prostate cancer.
Instead, a shared SYMPTOM TRIGGER (LUTS: nocturia, weak stream, pelvic/urinary pain) brings the man to
urology; the diagnostic work-up (PSA + DRE + TRUS, then mpMRI + biopsy if PSA elevated) then BRANCHES into
either benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) or prostate cancer (PCa). BPH is the diagnostic OCCASION, not the cause.
CALIBRATION: EAU-EANM-ESTRO-ESUR-ISUP-SIOG 2024 guideline provides the STRUCTURE of the pathway;
German S3-Leitlinie Prostatakarzinom v8.1 (2025) and German cancer-registry data (ZfKD/RKI 'Krebs in
Deutschland', ECIS) calibrate the transition PROBABILITIES. Every calibrated arrow carries a 'remarks'
citation; the full source trace is in epidemiology/prostate_calibration.md.
SCOPE: this is a PROTOTYPE (module-JSON only, not yet run). All terminology codes VALIDATED against
the CEIR-OS terminology server (SNOMED INT 20250701); full trace in terminology/snomed_data_dictionary.md.
Note: TRUS/mpMRI need prostate bodySite post-coordination; PI-RADS uses LOINC 82717-8 (no SNOMED).
COHORT DESIGN (deliberate selection, NOT epidemiology): 100% of males 50-60 present symptomatically to
urology (LUTS trigger). This defines a SELECTED symptomatic cohort for maximal pathway-trace yield.
All downstream probabilities are clinically calibrated - see remarks + epidemiology/prostate_calibration.md.

Medications are dual-coded WHO-ATC (http://www.whocc.no/atc, validated on tx.fhir.org) + ATC-DE/BfArM (http://fhir.de/CodeSystem/bfarm/atc, validated on MII termserver) per MII-Onko issue #283 (intl + national).

BCR->salvage: curatively treated patients enter PSA follow-up -> risk-dependent biochemical recurrence -> PSMA-PET -> salvage RT (post-RP) / salvage prostatectomy (post-RT) -> cured or systemic/metastatic. Codes validated (SNOMED INT). See epidemiology/prostate_calibration.md.
Only males proceed - prostate pathway.

Cohort = symptomatic men 50-60 presenting to urology. Every male reaching 50 presents with LUTS (100% presentation) - a deliberately SELECTED population for a high-yield test corpus, NOT an epidemiologically representative presentation rate.
Most, but not all, of the cohort is pinned to the 2018-2022 hospital-data window (see Year_Lottery).
0.85/0.15 split is a placeholder (🔴) - tune to reflect how much of your real population the Table 3
extract actually covers. The 0.15 'outside window' branch keeps the patient's own natural age-50
calendar date (whatever -a/-r produced) with no forcing - other years CAN occur. Those patients use
the generic (non-year-specific) 'Other' delay variants at each waiting-time step. See docs/time_variance.md §3.
0 is a sentinel (not a real year) meaning 'outside the 2018-2022 window'. Kept numeric, not a string,
so Attribute==<year> comparisons in the *_Wait_Router states never compare a String to a Number
(Synthea's Attribute condition throws a RuntimeException on a type mismatch instead of returning false).
TEMPORAL CALIBRATION (2026-09-03 addition): the reference hospital dataset (own hospital data, C61,
Table 3) covers 2018-2022. This guard + Year_Lottery below pin the cohort's presentation date to that
window, independent of the -a/-r CLI flags used to generate the population. A patient who reaches age
50 before 2018 simply waits here (forward-only) until the window opens. REQUIRES REFERENCE_DATE <=
20221231 for every patient's age-50 date to be reachable within the window - see docs/time_variance.md.
Non-uniform per-year weighting of the diagnosis/presentation year, mirroring real hospital registry
volume 2018-2022 (placeholder weights below - 🔴 REPLACE with your own per-year patient counts once
available; Table 3 only gives the 5-year aggregate, not a per-year split). Modelled as a sequential
lottery: at whichever year we actually arrive (>=2018, see Enter_Diagnosis_Window), 'settle' locks in
that year; 'defer' waits for the next year and re-enters this same lottery. This guarantees every
patient eventually settles (2022 is a forced catch-all) - no patient is ever stuck. Settle
probabilities are the target year-weight renormalised over the years still remaining:
See docs/time_variance.md for the full derivation and how to plug in your real annual counts.
Dispatches to a year-specific waiting-time distribution using the 'diagnosis_year' attribute set by
Year_Lottery / Set_Diagnosis_Year_Other. 'Initial diagnosis' per-year waiting time/appointment (own
Patients outside the window (no matching year) get the generic 5-yr-average variant. See docs/time_variance.md §3.
2020 has the longest wait of the 5 years in the source data - plausibly a COVID-era system-strain effect.
Generic fallback for patients outside the 2018-2022 window (see Cohort_Year_Branch) - uses the
Table 3 5-year average since no year-specific data applies.
Digital rectal exam. S3 v8.1 demoted DRE from first screening test but it remains part of work-up.
Split of symptomatic 50-60 men after PSA/DRE into 'benign, no biopsy indication' vs 'elevated PSA -> imaging/biopsy'.
Among symptomatic men the eventual diagnosis is overwhelmingly BPH; cancer is found only in the PSA-elevated minority
(LUTS is not itself a PCa risk factor per EAU). Calibrated to ~30% suspicious/elevated-PSA entering the imaging pathway
(BPH inflates PSA in symptomatic men, so higher than the ~5% healthy-population >3.2 ng/mL rate).
Source: PMC8317798 (LUTS cohort ~67% benign); EAU 2024 diagnostic pathway.

Negative biopsy in a symptomatic man with elevated PSA -> managed as BPH.
BPH management ladder (indicative textbook priors, EAU/AUA-aligned - flag as approximate, not registry):
~1/3 watchful waiting, ~1/2 medical therapy, ~15% surgery over time. Source: Medscape BPH mgmt, PMC7109311.
Watchful waiting for mild symptoms (IPSS<=7). Validated SNOMED INT 20250701.
First-line alpha-1-blocker for moderate-severe LUTS. SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
5-ARI added for enlarged gland (>40 mL) / progression risk (combination therapy). SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
Transurethral resection of prostate - benchmark BPH surgery. Validated SNOMED INT 20250701.
Incidental prostate cancer in ~14% of TURP/HoLEP specimens (PMC12459874). These are typically low-grade,
incidentally-detected cancers -> route to the low-risk cancer node. The other 86% remain pure BPH.
EAU risk-group distribution at diagnosis, skewed toward LOCALIZED/lower grade for the 50-60 cohort
(younger men: more localized, M1 ~4% vs ~9% overall - SEER under-50 PMC11758148).
Base proportions from SEER/EAU classification (Xie PMC8076565) + grade migration (NCDB PMC10133398),
re-weighted younger. Low 0.32 / Intermediate 0.34 / High 0.17 / Locally-advanced 0.11 / Metastatic 0.06.
EAU low risk: PSA<10, ISUP 1 (Gleason 6), cT1-2a.

codes.display: Prostate specific Ag [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

remarks: EAU 2024: Active surveillance is the PREFERRED option for low-risk with life expectancy >10 yr (strong rec).
Validated SNOMED INT 20250701.
Time-to-treatment-decision on active surveillance, GMF2 Triangular (non-uniform, patient variance instead
of a flat range): most conversions cluster around 2.5-3 yr (HAROW median time-to-treatment 33 mo RP /
38.5 mo RT, PMC8332563), long tail out to 5 yr matching 10-yr intervention-free survival ~34%.
See docs/time_variance.md and epidemiology/prostate_calibration.md §10/12.
~50% of AS patients receive definitive treatment within 5 years (PMC7407781; German HAROW AS PMC8332563).
Cancer-specific survival on AS remains ~99-100% at 5 yr, so no death arrow from the AS branch.
AS patient converting to definitive therapy - split RP vs radiotherapy.
EAU intermediate risk: PSA 10-20 OR ISUP 2-3 OR cT2b.

mHSPC: ADT backbone is mandatory (LHRH agonist). SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
EAU 2024 Part II: mHSPC ADT alone is NO LONGER standard - intensify with ARPI (doublet) or docetaxel.
Split ARPI 0.6 / docetaxel 0.4 (indicative).
Androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (abiraterone/enzalutamide/apalutamide/darolutamide). SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
Docetaxel chemotherapy (esp. high-volume disease). SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
Time on first-line systemic therapy before castration resistance. GMF2 Triangular (non-uniform):
median time-to-CRPC on ADT+ARPI/docetaxel is commonly ~1.5-2 yr in trial cohorts, with a tail to 3 yr
for slower progressors. See docs/time_variance.md.
Progression to mCRPC and second-line therapy vs stable disease. Distant-stage 5-yr relative survival is low
(~30% range, German NRW registry PubMed 39742793); the death arrow lives here.
mCRPC second line (cabazitaxel / Lu-177-PSMA / PARPi per biomarker). Cabazitaxel encoded. SNOMED substance code, validated INT 20250701.
Outcome after second-line mCRPC therapy: prostate-cancer death vs survival to end of simulation.
Post-curative PSA surveillance window before biochemical recurrence (BCR) may surface. GMF2 Triangular
(non-uniform): most BCR that occurs surfaces within the first 2 yr of surveillance (S3 Ch. 7 early-
detection intent of quarterly-then-annual PSA), long tail out to 4 yr. See docs/time_variance.md.
Biochemical recurrence after curative therapy, risk-dependent (S3 Ch. 7). High / locally-advanced ~40%,
low / intermediate ~20% (indicative 10-yr BCR ranges). Replaces the old direct 15%->metastatic jump.
Rising PSA = BCR. S3 def: post-RP confirmed PSA >0.2 x2 (Stmt 7.2); post-RT nadir+2 (Phoenix, Stmt 7.3).

codes.display: PSMA-PET - prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography

remarks: Salvage by prior modality: post-RP -> salvage RT (S3 7.14); post-RT -> salvage prostatectomy (S3 7.20).
Salvage radiotherapy, start early (PSA <0.5), >=66 Gy (S3 Empf. 7.14/7.18).
Add ADT to salvage RT if unfavorable (PSA>0.7, PSA-DT<12mo, Gleason 8-10): 6 or 24 mo (S3 7.15-7.17).
Salvage prostatectomy after RT recurrence (S3 Empf. 7.20).
Salvage durable biochemical control ~55% at 5 yr (early salvage RT); failure -> systemic/metastatic.
